text:
Alex Laferriere might be the hardest-working forward in the league with the least to show for it. The former Harvard winger and third-round pick is playing 19:24 a night for Los Angeles, he's on the ice for 72% of the Kings' power-play chances (up from 30%), and he's thrown 61 hits.

The chances are there. He has 57 shots and 8.4 expected goals, and has turned them into three goals, a 5.3% shooting rate against a talent range near 11%. Over his last ten games his own chances came to 6.1 expected goals against the 4.0 we'd expect, and the Kings piled up 19.2 expected goals with him on the ice against a usual 12.4. The return: one goal.

At 5v5 the Kings get 57% of the expected goals (chance quality) with him out there, ten points better than without him, and they've scored five fewer goals than those chances deserve. That's a lot of bad luck in 19 games, which is still a small sample. The underlying game says he belongs in this role. The scoring should start to say it too.
headline: Laferriere's chances are piling up unanswered
